forces.title: Agentic AI shifts content discovery from SEO to GEO
forces.description: The rise of agentic AI is fundamentally altering how online content is discovered, moving from traditional search engine optimization (SEO) to generative engine optimization (GEO). Businesses must adapt to be recognized by AI models that learn individual preferences, rather than relying on clicks. This represents a generational shift that demands rethinking how information is categorized online, pushing for clear, structured data readable by AI.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Higher energy costs erode margins for TMT infrastructure
forces.description: Increased European gas prices are translating into higher electricity costs, impacting TMT companies, including those involved in media infrastructure. Energy is a core cost input for these businesses, and rising prices erode profit margins. This also risks delaying investment decisions, thereby dampening expansion appetite across the sector.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Agentic AI driven commerce reshaping content discoverability
forces.description: Agentic AI is transforming how consumers discover, engage, and shop online, leading to a significant shift in commerce. Brands must prioritize "generative engine optimization" (GEO) to ensure their content and products are prominently and accurately surfaced by AI shopping agents. This necessitates understanding consumer use of these agents, creating a new paradigm for content strategy, digital advertising, and platform monetization within Internet Platforms & Digital Media.
forces.source_title: Freshening up: A new winning formula for home and hygiene players

forces.title: Agentic AI and zero-click results reducing organic web traffic
forces.description: The emergence of agentic AI is transforming customer experiences, leading to a significant increase in "zero-click" search results. A Bain & Company survey in late 2024 revealed that 80% of consumers rely on zero-click results in at least 40% of their searches, consequently reducing organic web traffic by an estimated 15% to 25%. This shift fundamentally impacts search, social, and content platforms, altering user engagement and ad-driven monetization models.
forces.source_title: How Agentic AI Is Transforming Customer Experiences

forces.title: Generative AI enhancing digital marketing and personalization
forces.description: Generative AI offers numerous applications that boost digital marketing and personalized customer engagement. These include 1:1 marketing, product recommendations, AI-driven ad copywriting, social media engagement, and real-time content creation. Additionally, GenAI supports tailored product descriptions and improved product search ranking. These capabilities represent a strong tailwind for digital advertising and content platforms, increasing the demand for sophisticated, AI-enabled solutions within the Internet Platforms & Digital Media sector.
forces.source_title: Southeast Asia: What's Happening with Consumers and Consumer Products

forces.title: Automation and AI impacting graduate hiring in tech sector
forces.description: The tech sector in Ireland is experiencing a drop in graduate hiring, as companies increasingly automate routine tasks like payroll and credit control. This trend, highlighted by the Morgan McKinley Employment Monitor, suggests a shift towards AI-driven operations. While it aims for efficiency, it poses a long-term challenge to the talent pipeline for mid-level roles across the broader TMT sector, including Internet Platforms & Digital Media companies relying on tech talent.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: Vulnerability to global market sentiment in VC funding
forces.description: Ireland's venture capital funding environment is highly susceptible to global market sentiment, as evidenced by the sharp decline in Q2 2025 due to retracting international investors. This dependency on external capital flows poses a significant risk to indigenous startups across the TMT sector, including Internet Platforms & Digital Media companies, and underscores the urgent need to build domestic funding capacity to support local innovation and growth.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: Internet advertising driven by personalization and penetration
forces.description: The internet advertising sector in Ireland is projected for rapid expansion, with revenue forecasted to grow at a 9.2% CAGR to €1.8 billion by 2029. This growth is primarily driven by increased internet penetration and the enhanced capabilities of AI-enabled hyper-personalization in targeted advertising. Digital video advertising, in particular, is expected to be the fastest-growing category, representing a significant tailwind for the Digital Advertising & Ad Tech segment (IN090302).
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: Agentic AI enabling autonomous decision-making and digital labor
forces.description: Agentic AI is emerging as the "next big thing," distinct from Generative AI by its ability to act autonomously, make decisions, assess situations, plan, and execute tasks with minimal human intervention. This 'digital labor' promises infinite potential for optimization and automation of routine tasks, transforming business operations. For Internet Platforms & Digital Media, this represents a profound structural shift in how services are delivered, customer interactions are managed, and efficiencies are achieved.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: AI limitations and ethical concerns hinder widespread impact
forces.description: Despite the rapid advancements in AI, its actual impact on business revenue remains limited, with issues persisting in reproducibility, explainability, and data quality. There's a significant risk that AI systems could amplify inherent biases and make opaque decisions if not properly governed. For Internet Platforms & Digital Media, managing these limitations and establishing ethical frameworks are crucial to ensure transparency, accountability, and fairness, preventing potential negative societal and business outcomes from AI deployment.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: European Accessibility Act imposes new digital platform compliance
forces.description: The European Accessibility Act (EAA), effective June 2025, mandates new accessibility standards across digital platforms, financial services, and public transport. This regulation, while aiming to enhance inclusion for persons with disabilities, imposes new compliance requirements for businesses and service providers, including Internet Platforms & Digital Media companies. This represents a structural change, necessitating platform adjustments to meet these new standards and potentially incurring costs for development and implementation.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Healthcare H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: Precision influencer marketing boosts brand engagement and sales
forces.description: Influencer marketing is evolving into a powerful force, reshaping consumer-brand interactions and driving tailored engagements with measurable outcomes. Precision influencer marketing campaigns are six times more efficient at reaching target shoppers than traditional efforts, boosting sales by up to 20% in the first month. This trend represents a significant tailwind for Search, Social & Content Platforms (IN090301) and Digital Advertising & Ad Tech (IN090302), increasing demand for data-driven influencer strategies and tools that leverage these platforms.

forces.title: Traditional influencer campaigns face engagement and ROI transparency issues
forces.description: Many traditional influencer marketing campaigns are struggling to connect effectively with target consumers and lack transparency regarding their return on investment. This challenge leads to wasted marketing expenditure and potential brand damage, presenting a headwind for less sophisticated digital advertising approaches. The difficulties highlight the urgent need for a shift towards more precise, data-driven influencer strategies and advanced ad tech solutions that can offer clearer attribution and better audience targeting within the Internet Platforms & Digital Media sector.

viewpoints.title: Venture capital investment in Irish TMT sector strengthened in early 2026
viewpoints.description: Irish venture capital investment saw a substantial uplift in Q1 2026, with 19 deals closing for $212.3 million, up from $155.1 million in Q4 2025. The Telecoms/Tech Services sector was particularly active, ranking second with 15 deals, showing resilience despite global uncertainty. Investor interest remains strong, especially in AI, with a clear shift towards larger, later-stage investments. This indicates a cautiously positive outlook for funding in the broader TMT space, which includes Internet Platforms & Digital Media.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: Online consumption now dominant for news, driving digital-first models
viewpoints.description: Data from Core, Ireland's largest marketing communications firm, indicates that 2024 marked a major shift where online consumption became the dominant source of news, surpassing traditional media like radio, television, newspapers, and social media. This reinforces the critical need for digital-first operating models across the media landscape. For Internet Platforms & Digital Media, this trend signifies a positive and sustained shift in audience attention towards digital channels, supporting platforms monetized via advertising.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

viewpoints.title: AI adoption in Irish businesses remains in early stages despite hype
viewpoints.description: Despite significant hype surrounding AI, surveys from PwC, Accenture, and Trinity College indicate that while nearly all Irish businesses have started their AI journey, only a small percentage (6-8%) have deployed the technology at scale. Most organizations are relying on third-party solutions, suggesting that the sector is still in the early stages of unlocking AI's full potential. This indicates a cautious but developing stance on widespread AI integration within businesses, including those utilizing Internet Platforms & Digital Media.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

viewpoints.title: Irish SME venture capital funding plummeted in Q2 2025
viewpoints.description: Venture capital funding for Irish SMEs dramatically fell to €112.6 million in Q2 2025, the lowest level in ten years, according to the Irish Venture Capital Association (IVCA). This sharp decline, attributed to retracting international investors and a loss of €305 million in investment, highlights Ireland's vulnerability to global market sentiment. This represents a negative outlook for indigenous startups, including those within Internet Platforms & Digital Media, unless domestic funding capacity is built.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

demand_drivers.driver: Social media influence on travel inspiration
demand_drivers.description: Platforms like Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube significantly influence travel planning, particularly for younger demographics (18-34 years old), driving engagement and potential ad revenue for these platforms (45-46% cite as top source).

demand_drivers.driver: Search engine influence on travel inspiration
demand_drivers.description: Search engines remain a relevant source of travel inspiration across all age groups, with 41% of respondents citing them as a key source, contributing to traffic and monetization for search platforms.

market_sizing.methodology: McKinsey Consumer Survey on airline retailing preferences (Mar 2025, n=7,000) shows influence of different platforms on travel inspiration.
